name: Vanquish Attach Me – Order & Product Attachments for WooCommerce
author: Vanquish

sections.description:
Vanquish Attach Me for WooCommerce lets you give each customer the files that belong to their order, straight from the order screen: the proof they have to approve, their invoice, a certificate, the finished design. They find them on their order page and in the order emails, behind private download links. Files that belong to a whole product — a manual, a size chart, a data sheet — work the same way, on the product page, after purchase, or both. Upload the file, pick one from the media library, or point at a URL.

Uploaded files are not left where a URL can find them: they sit behind server rules and an unguessable path, and they are served through an endpoint that checks who is asking — the customer who placed that order, or somebody who can manage the shop. That is not a setting you can turn off — it is the only correct way to serve a file attached to an order, so it is simply how the plugin works.

Large files go up in pieces, so your server’s per-request upload limit is not the limit on what you can attach.

Proofs: file approval with your customer (Premium). Send a design, a print layout or a translation from the order for the customer to approve. They approve or reject it on their order page and you write to each other; every new version asks for approval again, and the whole history stays on the order. Reminders, automatic approval after a number of days, and a one-click import from the CodeCanyon plugin WooCommerce File Approval.

Free features

  • Attach any number of files to an order: upload them, choose them from the media library, or link to an external URL.
  • A title and a description for each file, shown to the customer.
  • Attach files to products, with a choice of which variations they apply to.
  • Show a product’s files on the product page, on the order page after buying, or both.
  • Files attached to the standard WooCommerce emails (processing, completed, invoice, refunded) and to custom emails registered by other plugins, chosen per file.
  • A block inside the order emails with your own wording and the download links, with placeholders for [order_number], [customer_name] and [order_page_link] that a click writes into the text.
  • Choose the order statuses in which each file is available; in the others it stays hidden.
  • Default options: the emails, the statuses it is available in and the email block a new attachment starts with, set once instead of on every file, for order attachments, product attachments or both.
  • A list you can read at a glance: each file is a row that shows its type, its size and what is set on it — the emails it goes with, where it shows, when it expires. Open a row to edit it, drop files on the list to add them.
  • The largest file to attach to an email, set once: a bigger file goes out as a download link in the same email, so an oversized attachment never costs the customer the whole message.
  • Files keep the name they were uploaded with, on the order, in the download and in the email. The copy on your server keeps its unguessable name.
  • Each file’s type and size under its name — “PDF · 2.4 MB” — so the customer knows what they are about to open.
  • Image previews, at a thumbnail size you choose, and a configurable position for the attachments box on the order page.
  • A “View attachments” button in the customer’s order list.
  • A product’s files in a tab of their own, or beside the price: under the short description or after the “Add to cart” button — chosen for the whole shop, and per file where one belongs somewhere else.
  • Sections on the product page — “Manuals”, “Certificates” — optionally folded, and a choice of cards or a compact list.
  • A Product attachments block, for a block theme’s product template or any page: the current product’s files, or any product’s.
  • An attachments column in the admin orders list, a “Manage” modal for handling them without opening the order, a filter for orders that have attachments, and a bulk action to delete them. The products list has the same bulk action.
  • Every customer-facing text is editable — and, with WPML or Polylang active, editable per language.
  • Template overrides from your theme, HPOS (High-Performance Order Storage) support.
  • Migrates automatically from the legacy “WooCommerce Attach Me!” (CodeCanyon) plugin: settings, product attachments and every order’s files.

Premium features

  • Bulk product attachments — one rule attaches a file to many products or categories at once: all products, only the ones you pick, or all except those, with or without child categories. The rule counts the products it reaches as you build it, and can be duplicated. No opening a thousand products.
  • Bulk order attachments — one file for the orders you pick by number, or for every order: terms and conditions, a warranty, a notice. Kept once in its rule, shown next to each order’s own files and sent with the emails you choose. Every product and order lists the bulk attachments that reach it.
  • Proofs / approval requests — send a file from the order for the customer to approve: a design, a print layout, a translation, uploaded or picked from the media library. They approve or reject it on their order page, you write to each other, and every new version you send asks for approval again, with the whole history kept. The customer can add files to their answers. Their verdict can move the order to another status; emails to each side are grouped, so three files sent in a row make one email. Reminders when nobody answers, and automatic approval after a number of days, announced to the customer beforehand. A “Files to approve” page in My account, and every proof of every order in one list.
  • Expiry — a file that stops being available on a fixed date, or a set time after the order. It disappears from the order page, the download link stops working, and the file can be deleted from the server automatically.
  • All attachments — every order’s files on one screen: search by file, order or customer, see which nobody has downloaded yet and which expire this week, and delete in bulk — every expired file in one click. A second tab lists every file sent for approval: what is waiting, rejected and approved.
  • Clean up old orders — free disk space by deleting the attachments and proofs of orders placed before a date, or more than three months to two years ago, in the statuses you choose. The page says how many orders it is about before anything is deleted, asks you to confirm, works a few orders at a time and carries on from where it stopped if a request fails. The same cleanup can run by itself every night. Each order keeps a note of what was removed.
  • Download history — see on every order whether the customer has downloaded each file, and when: under the file’s name, in full when you open it, and as an order note the first time. No IP address or other personal data is kept.
  • Download limits and a required disclaimer — a maximum number of downloads per file, and terms the customer must accept before the first one.
  • Visibility by user role, including visitors who are not signed in, on product attachments and bulk product attachments.
  • Automatic email files — a file that goes out with every copy of a chosen email, whatever the order contains: terms on every invoice, a returns form on every completed order. Any email WooCommerce sends to a customer, including the ones about an account rather than an order: new account, password reset.
  • A message written by hand — send the customer an email from the order screen, with whichever of that order’s files you choose attached or linked, in your shop’s own email template. Preview it before it goes; it leaves an order note saying what went out.
  • A library of preset texts — messages written once and offered under every editor by an “Insert template” button, so a shop that says the same thing on every order writes it once.
  • CSV import — one row, one link, one order or one product (by id or SKU), for a shop that already has its files listed somewhere else. Drag the file in; comma, semicolon or tab separated.
  • My Account → Downloads — the attachments listed on the page that claims to list everything the customer can download.
  • Shortcodes — put the attachments, or a single download link, on a page of your own. Each shows nothing at all unless the person reading the page is entitled to that order.
  • Files only in the emails — a product file, or a bulk product attachment, that goes out with the order emails you pick and shows nowhere on the site: not on the order page, not on the product page.
  • Copy the download link with one click, on the customer’s side.
  • Premium default options — what a new proof starts with, the download terms and the copy-link button, and the manual message to the customer, set once.
  • Mark up the proof — the customer circles, points and writes their corrections right on an image proof, with a pen, arrows, boxes and notes, and the drawing goes with their answer. Off until you switch it on, for every file or only the ones you choose.
  • Moving from WooCommerce File Approval — its files, conversations, customers’ files, answers, settings and preset answers become proofs, from one button.
  • Works with Vanquish Upload Files — the customer uploads their artwork with Upload Files, you press “Send a proof” on that file, and the proof form opens here, filled in. The state of the proof then shows next to the file, for you and for your customer.

Screenshots, plans and answers on the plugin’s page: vanquishplugins.com/plugins/attach-me.

External services

The free version does not send any data to external services. Files you upload stay on your own server, and the download links point at your own site.

This plugin uses Freemius to manage licensing and updates for the premium version, and to offer an optional opt-in when you first activate it. Nothing is sent unless you opt in or activate a licence; if you do, Freemius receives your site URL, WordPress and PHP versions and your administrator email address, in order to deliver updates and support. See freemius.com, its terms and its privacy policy.

The premium version adds no external services of its own: bulk product attachments, approval, expiry, automatic emails and the manual notification all run on your site, and the emails go out through WooCommerce.

More WooCommerce plugins by Vanquish

  • Vanquish Upload Files for WooCommerce – let customers upload files (even large ones) on the product, cart, checkout and order pages, for custom, personalized and print-on-demand products.
  • Vanquish Shipping Tracking for WooCommerce – tracking numbers on orders and emails, with 1,600+ carriers and their logos, a direct tracking link and a Track button. No account needed.
  • Vanquish Multiple Addresses for WooCommerce – give customers an address book: save multiple billing and shipping addresses and pick one at checkout.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to the /wp-content/plugins/vanquish-attach-me-for-woocommerce directory, or install the plugin through the WordPress plugins screen.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ screen in WordPress.
  3. Make sure WooCommerce is installed and active.
  4. Configure the plugin from the “Attach Me” menu.
sections.faq:
Where are the uploaded files kept?

In a folder inside your uploads directory, three ways round at once. The plugin writes the rules that close a directory to direct access, in the forms Apache and IIS understand. Because nginx honours neither, the path is unguessable as well: each order’s files sit under a directory name derived from a secret the plugin generates for your site, rather than from the order number, and every stored file keeps its own name with twelve random characters added.

And the way in is the only way in: every download goes through a signed link, which checks whether the person asking placed that order or can manage the shop.

There is no switch for any of this. A file attached to an order is private by definition, and an option to serve it insecurely would only ever be turned on by mistake.

Can I attach a file that is bigger than my server’s upload limit?

Yes. Files are sent to the server in pieces small enough to clear upload_max_filesize and post_max_size, so neither caps what you can attach. The screen shows the maximum it will accept.

What about files in the media library, or on another server?

Both work. A media library file keeps its own public address in wp-content/uploads — that is how the media library works — so if a file must not be reachable by anyone holding its URL, upload it through the plugin instead of adding it to the library. An external URL is only ever a link: the plugin does not fetch somebody else’s file to attach it to your emails.

Does it work with HPOS (High-Performance Order Storage)?

Yes, with HPOS and with the classic order storage.

I am migrating from the CodeCanyon “WooCommerce Attach Me!” plugin. Do I lose anything?

No. Your settings, your texts, the files on your products and the files on every order are converted for you. The importer runs from Attach Me → Settings → Import old data, a tab that appears as soon as the old plugin’s data is found. It shows how much is left as it goes, and finishes in the background if you close the tab. An order is also converted the first time somebody opens it, whatever happened before.

Your files stay where they are on disk and keep working, and the old plugin’s download links are still understood. A customer with an account follows one after signing in, and so do you.

A link to a guest order’s file needs one thing more than the link. Those old URLs were built as ?wcam_id=<order number>-<0, 1, 2...>, which anybody can type out, and a guest order has no account to check the visitor against — so on its own such a link is not proof of anything, and is refused. It works when the request also carries the order key, which is the token WooCommerce puts in the order links it emails: following the file from the customer’s own order page works, pasting the bare old URL does not.

The old plugin’s data is left in place rather than deleted, so nothing is destroyed by importing. You can keep both installed while you check the result, then deactivate the old one.

I use the CodeCanyon “WooCommerce File Approval” plugin. Can I move?

Yes: proofs are its successor, in Premium. Under Attach Me → Settings → Proofs / File approval, a card appears on any site that has its data, and imports it in one go: each file becomes a proof on its order, with its conversation, the files the customer sent and the customer’s answer, each with its date. Its settings and preset answers can come along too. Nothing of the old plugin is changed or deleted, and the import can be run again: what was already imported is skipped.

File Approval replaced a file when a new one was sent and kept no history of it, so each proof starts with one version: the file as it is now. The files your customers sent are copied into the protected folder; File Approval kept them in a public one.

Do the premium features change how the free ones behave?

No. The premium package is the same plugin with more in it. Everything described above under “free features” works the same either way, and the settings you have already made are untouched by activating a licence.

How much does Premium cost, and how do I get it?

There are monthly, yearly and lifetime plans, for one site up to ten. The current prices are on the pricing page.

To order, install and activate the free version, then go to Attach Me → Upgrade in your WordPress admin. The plans and a secure checkout, handled by Freemius, are right there, and the same screen walks you through activating Premium on your site.

Can I try the plugin before buying Premium?

Yes, and it is strongly recommended. The free version on WordPress.org is the same plugin with fewer features: install it on your own site, with your own theme, and check that the attachments look right on your order pages, your product pages and in your emails before upgrading. Premium adds features on top of it, on the same foundations.

Can my customers draw their corrections on the file?

Yes, in Premium, on an image proof. Under the file the customer finds a Mark up button: it opens the image full screen, where they can draw freehand, add arrows, boxes, circles and notes in four colours, and undo what they do not like. The drawing is saved as a PNG of the proof with the marks on it, and goes with their answer — “Request changes”, say — or as a message on its own. You see it in the conversation, like any other file they send.

It is off until you switch it on, under Attach Me → Settings → Proofs / File approval → Files from the customer → Mark up. That switch is where each new file to approve starts; any one file can then have it on or off on its own, from the gear beside it on the order screen. It works with customers’ uploads off too. Images only for now: not PDF.

Why do the emails about proofs arrive a few minutes late?

On purpose. When something happens on a proof, the email is not sent at once: it goes about two minutes later, and everything that happens on the same order in the meantime goes into that one email. Three files uploaded one after another, or an answer followed by a second message, make one email instead of three. This is Premium, as proofs are.

You choose the wait under Attach Me → Settings → Proofs / File approval → Emails to the customer → When they go: at once, or after 2, 5 or 10 minutes. “At once” sends one email for each thing that happens. The same wait applies to the emails to the shop.

The send is queued with Action Scheduler, the queue WooCommerce itself uses: each one is listed under Tools → Scheduled Actions, hook vanam_proof_notify. On a site with few visitors the queue only runs when someone opens a page, so the two minutes can become more. A real server cron that calls wp-cron.php every minute keeps it on time.

For a wait the option does not offer, use the vanam_proof_notify_delay filter, in seconds. It starts from the option and has the last word:

add_filter( 'vanam_proof_notify_delay', function () { return 30; } );

My mail server refuses large attachments. What can I do?

Set Attach Me → Settings → General → Emails → Largest file to attach. A file over that size is not attached: the email carries a download link to it instead, in the same place as the other links. Files under it are attached as before.

Can I change the wording the customer sees?

Yes, under Attach Me → Settings → Texts: the titles of the boxes and of the product tab, the download buttons, the message when there are no files and the “View attachments” button, and in Premium every text of the proofs and of their emails. The text above the download links in the order emails is set in Default options → Download links in order emails, and on each order. With WPML or Polylang active, the Texts tab shows one language at a time, with the default language’s wording under each field.

What happens if I uninstall the plugin?

Nothing of yours is removed. Your settings and your wording stay, the files attached to your orders and products stay, and the files on disk are left alone — so reinstalling puts you back exactly where you were. Only two things go: the plugin’s scheduled events, which would otherwise keep firing for a plugin that is no longer installed, and its caches, which would expire on their own anyway.

1.7.1

  • New (Premium): choose when the emails about proofs go out, under Proofs / File approval › Emails to the customer › When they go: at once, or after 2, 5 or 10 minutes. The wait gathers what happens on an order into one email; 2 minutes, as before, unless you change it. The vanam_proof_notify_delay filter still works, and has the last word.
  • New (Premium): choose the tab the order’s “Files & proofs” box opens on, under Proofs / File approval › Order screen: the last tab used, as before, or always Files, or always Proofs. A link to a tab still opens that tab.
  • Developers: the vanam_order_metabox_first_tab filter sets the tab the box opens on.

1.7.0

  • New (Premium): Mark up. Under an image proof the customer finds a “Mark up” button that opens the file full screen, with a pen, arrows, boxes, circles, notes, four colours and undo. The drawing is saved as a PNG of the proof with the marks on it, and goes with their answer or as a message, where you see it in the conversation. Switch it on in Proofs / File approval › Files from the customer; it works with customers’ uploads off too. Images only for now, not PDF.
  • New (Premium): Mark up file by file. The switch on the Proofs tab is what each new file to approve starts with; any file can have it on or off on its own, in its settings (the gear beside it on the order screen). Files sent before 1.7.0 follow the switch.
  • New (Premium): three new texts for it on the Texts tab, under Proofs › On the order page › Mark up.

1.6.5

  • New (Premium): developers can add to the customer’s proof screen without overriding its template. The actions vanam_proof_customer_preview_after and vanam_proof_customer_form_fields, the vanam_proof_card_ready event, and window.vanamProofCustomer, which starts an answer and attaches a file to it: for example a markup tool that sends the customer’s drawing with their rejection. They are listed in includes/api.php.
  • Changed (Premium): the template premium/proofs.php has the new actions, and data attributes on each card. A copy in a theme needs them for the above.

1.6.4

  • Changed: the plugin’s homepage, linked from the Plugins screen, is now its page on vanquishplugins.com, with screenshots, plans and answers.

Vanquish Upload Files uses them for “Send a proof” on a file the customer uploaded.
  • Changed (Premium): an automatic approval fires the vanam_proof_event action like every other answer. It sends no extra email.

1.6.2

  • New (Premium): “Only in the emails”, a switch under the emails of a product file and of a bulk product rule. The file goes out with those emails and shows nowhere on the site. Files that arrived that way from the CodeCanyon plugin say so on their row, in the free version too.

The texts are grouped in the order the customer meets them, each group says how many have been changed, and one search covers them all; “Customised only” shows what you changed, and each changed text has a button back to the default. On a multilingual site one language shows at a time, with the default language’s wording under each field. The email texts have their placeholders as buttons.

  • New: an order and a product now list the bulk attachments that reach them, under their own files, with a link to the rules (Premium).
  • New: with WPML or Polylang, a bulk attachment’s name and description can be written in every language of the shop, one field per language as on the Texts tab (Premium). A language left empty shows the default one.
  • New: the CSV import (Premium) takes product rows as well as order rows: a product by id or SKU, with optional visibility, position and section columns. A variation gets the file on its parent, for that variation only. Drag the file onto the page; a comma, semicolon or tab separator is recognised on its own, and a sample file can be downloaded.
  • Changed: “Bulk product attachments” and “Import from CSV” are now one menu entry, Bulk attachments, with Products, Orders and CSV import tabs (Premium). The old import address leads to its tab.
  • Improved: on the products list, a paperclip heads the attachments column instead of a word that broke the table.
  • Improved: an attachment’s fields are grouped under small headings — Content, File, Who sees it and where — instead of being ruled off one by one, on the order screen, the product screen and the bulk product attachments screen.
  • Fixed: on the product screen, “Where the customer sees it” sat glued to the emails below it.
  • Developers: each file on the product page is drawn by a new template, product/attachment.php; product/tab.php arranges them. A copy of tab.php from an earlier version keeps working.

1.2.0

  • New: each file’s type and size under its name on the order page and the product page, as in “PDF · 2.4 MB”. On by default; switch it off under General → How each file is shown.
  • New: a product’s files can sit under the short description or after the “Add to cart” button instead of in their own tab (General → Product page).
  • New: download history (Premium). See on every order whether the customer has downloaded each file and when, with an order note the first time. The free version already records it, so the history is there whenever you upgrade.
  • Changed: downloads by the shop’s own staff are no longer counted. Opening a customer’s link to check a file used to count as a download, and used up one of the customer’s downloads on a file with a limit.
  • Improved: the attachments box on the order screen is three separate sections — the files, the download links in the order emails, and the message to the customer — each with its own button. The email block’s text and statuses only appear while it is switched on.
  • Improved: customer approval offers Yes and No only (Premium). A submission with no answer and no comment is ignored, instead of sending the shop a “Not yet” note and email.
  • Fixed: on sites hosted on Windows, an uploaded file was never attached: the upload finished, and the attachment was not created.
  • Fixed: when saving an attachment failed, the reason is shown instead of “Something went wrong”.
  • Fixed: the message to the customer in the orders list’s “Manage” window had no text editor (Premium).

1.1.0

  • New: Default options tab. Choose the emails, hidden statuses and email block a new attachment starts with, for order attachments, product attachments or both. Premium adds defaults for customer approval, the download terms, the copy-link button and the manual message to the customer. Settings imported from “WooCommerce Attach Me!” now include its default options.
  • New: an attachment’s less common settings sit in a collapsible “Advanced options” section, and options that depend on another one only appear once it is switched on.
  • Improved: “Bulk rules” is now called “Bulk product attachments” (Premium).
  • Improved: the files offered in the manual message to the customer are switches, and can start all selected, with a confirmation before sending a message with no files (Premium).

1.0.1

  • Fixed: on stores using the classic order storage (HPOS switched off), the importer counted every order as legacy data, showed the import notice on sites that never had the old plugin, and could keep running without finishing.
  • Fixed: the automatic deletion of expired files (Premium) stopped after the first 200 orders with attachments.

1.0.0

  • First release. A rewrite from scratch of the CodeCanyon “WooCommerce Attach Me!” plugin, with an automatic importer for its settings, product attachments and order files.
  • Uploaded files are served from a protected folder through a signed, access-checked endpoint, always — not as an option.
  • Chunked uploads, so the server’s per-request limit is not the limit on attachment size.
  • HPOS support, template overrides, and every customer-facing text editable per language with WPML or Polylang.

short_description: Order and product attachments for WooCommerce: attach files, show them to the customer and send them with the order emails.
description:
Vanquish Attach Me for WooCommerce lets you give each customer the files that belong to their order, straight from the order screen: the proof they have to approve, their invoice, a certificate, the finished design. They find them on their order page and in the order emails, behind private download links. Files that belong to a whole product — a manual, a size chart, a data sheet — work the same way, on the product page, after purchase, or both. Upload the file, pick one from the media library, or point at a URL.

Uploaded files are not left where a URL can find them: they sit behind server rules and an unguessable path, and they are served through an endpoint that checks who is asking — the customer who placed that order, or somebody who can manage the shop. That is not a setting you can turn off — it is the only correct way to serve a file attached to an order, so it is simply how the plugin works.

Large files go up in pieces, so your server’s per-request upload limit is not the limit on what you can attach.

Proofs: file approval with your customer (Premium). Send a design, a print layout or a translation from the order for the customer to approve. They approve or reject it on their order page and you write to each other; every new version asks for approval again, and the whole history stays on the order. Reminders, automatic approval after a number of days, and a one-click import from the CodeCanyon plugin WooCommerce File Approval.

Free features

  • Attach any number of files to an order: upload them, choose them from the media library, or link to an external URL.
  • A title and a description for each file, shown to the customer.
  • Attach files to products, with a choice of which variations they apply to.
  • Show a product’s files on the product page, on the order page after buying, or both.
  • Files attached to the standard WooCommerce emails (processing, completed, invoice, refunded) and to custom emails registered by other plugins, chosen per file.
  • A block inside the order emails with your own wording and the download links, with placeholders for [order_number], [customer_name] and [order_page_link] that a click writes into the text.
  • Choose the order statuses in which each file is available; in the others it stays hidden.
  • Default options: the emails, the statuses it is available in and the email block a new attachment starts with, set once instead of on every file, for order attachments, product attachments or both.
  • A list you can read at a glance: each file is a row that shows its type, its size and what is set on it — the emails it goes with, where it shows, when it expires. Open a row to edit it, drop files on the list to add them.
  • The largest file to attach to an email, set once: a bigger file goes out as a download link in the same email, so an oversized attachment never costs the customer the whole message.
  • Files keep the name they were uploaded with, on the order, in the download and in the email. The copy on your server keeps its unguessable name.
  • Each file’s type and size under its name — “PDF · 2.4 MB” — so the customer knows what they are about to open.
  • Image previews, at a thumbnail size you choose, and a configurable position for the attachments box on the order page.
  • A “View attachments” button in the customer’s order list.
  • A product’s files in a tab of their own, or beside the price: under the short description or after the “Add to cart” button — chosen for the whole shop, and per file where one belongs somewhere else.
  • Sections on the product page — “Manuals”, “Certificates” — optionally folded, and a choice of cards or a compact list.
  • A Product attachments block, for a block theme’s product template or any page: the current product’s files, or any product’s.
  • An attachments column in the admin orders list, a “Manage” modal for handling them without opening the order, a filter for orders that have attachments, and a bulk action to delete them. The products list has the same bulk action.
  • Every customer-facing text is editable — and, with WPML or Polylang active, editable per language.
  • Template overrides from your theme, HPOS (High-Performance Order Storage) support.
  • Migrates automatically from the legacy “WooCommerce Attach Me!” (CodeCanyon) plugin: settings, product attachments and every order’s files.

Premium features

  • Bulk product attachments — one rule attaches a file to many products or categories at once: all products, only the ones you pick, or all except those, with or without child categories. The rule counts the products it reaches as you build it, and can be duplicated. No opening a thousand products.
  • Bulk order attachments — one file for the orders you pick by number, or for every order: terms and conditions, a warranty, a notice. Kept once in its rule, shown next to each order’s own files and sent with the emails you choose. Every product and order lists the bulk attachments that reach it.
  • Proofs / approval requests — send a file from the order for the customer to approve: a design, a print layout, a translation, uploaded or picked from the media library. They approve or reject it on their order page, you write to each other, and every new version you send asks for approval again, with the whole history kept. The customer can add files to their answers. Their verdict can move the order to another status; emails to each side are grouped, so three files sent in a row make one email. Reminders when nobody answers, and automatic approval after a number of days, announced to the customer beforehand. A “Files to approve” page in My account, and every proof of every order in one list.
  • Expiry — a file that stops being available on a fixed date, or a set time after the order. It disappears from the order page, the download link stops working, and the file can be deleted from the server automatically.
  • All attachments — every order’s files on one screen: search by file, order or customer, see which nobody has downloaded yet and which expire this week, and delete in bulk — every expired file in one click. A second tab lists every file sent for approval: what is waiting, rejected and approved.
  • Clean up old orders — free disk space by deleting the attachments and proofs of orders placed before a date, or more than three months to two years ago, in the statuses you choose. The page says how many orders it is about before anything is deleted, asks you to confirm, works a few orders at a time and carries on from where it stopped if a request fails. The same cleanup can run by itself every night. Each order keeps a note of what was removed.
  • Download history — see on every order whether the customer has downloaded each file, and when: under the file’s name, in full when you open it, and as an order note the first time. No IP address or other personal data is kept.
  • Download limits and a required disclaimer — a maximum number of downloads per file, and terms the customer must accept before the first one.
  • Visibility by user role, including visitors who are not signed in, on product attachments and bulk product attachments.
  • Automatic email files — a file that goes out with every copy of a chosen email, whatever the order contains: terms on every invoice, a returns form on every completed order. Any email WooCommerce sends to a customer, including the ones about an account rather than an order: new account, password reset.
  • A message written by hand — send the customer an email from the order screen, with whichever of that order’s files you choose attached or linked, in your shop’s own email template. Preview it before it goes; it leaves an order note saying what went out.
  • A library of preset texts — messages written once and offered under every editor by an “Insert template” button, so a shop that says the same thing on every order writes it once.
  • CSV import — one row, one link, one order or one product (by id or SKU), for a shop that already has its files listed somewhere else. Drag the file in; comma, semicolon or tab separated.
  • My Account → Downloads — the attachments listed on the page that claims to list everything the customer can download.
  • Shortcodes — put the attachments, or a single download link, on a page of your own. Each shows nothing at all unless the person reading the page is entitled to that order.
  • Files only in the emails — a product file, or a bulk product attachment, that goes out with the order emails you pick and shows nowhere on the site: not on the order page, not on the product page.
  • Copy the download link with one click, on the customer’s side.
  • Premium default options — what a new proof starts with, the download terms and the copy-link button, and the manual message to the customer, set once.
  • Mark up the proof — the customer circles, points and writes their corrections right on an image proof, with a pen, arrows, boxes and notes, and the drawing goes with their answer. Off until you switch it on, for every file or only the ones you choose.
  • Moving from WooCommerce File Approval — its files, conversations, customers’ files, answers, settings and preset answers become proofs, from one button.
  • Works with Vanquish Upload Files — the customer uploads their artwork with Upload Files, you press “Send a proof” on that file, and the proof form opens here, filled in. The state of the proof then shows next to the file, for you and for your customer.

Screenshots, plans and answers on the plugin’s page: vanquishplugins.com/plugins/attach-me.

External services

The free version does not send any data to external services. Files you upload stay on your own server, and the download links point at your own site.

This plugin uses Freemius to manage licensing and updates for the premium version, and to offer an optional opt-in when you first activate it. Nothing is sent unless you opt in or activate a licence; if you do, Freemius receives your site URL, WordPress and PHP versions and your administrator email address, in order to deliver updates and support. See freemius.com, its terms and its privacy policy.

The premium version adds no external services of its own: bulk product attachments, approval, expiry, automatic emails and the manual notification all run on your site, and the emails go out through WooCommerce.

More WooCommerce plugins by Vanquish

  • Vanquish Upload Files for WooCommerce – let customers upload files (even large ones) on the product, cart, checkout and order pages, for custom, personalized and print-on-demand products.
  • Vanquish Shipping Tracking for WooCommerce – tracking numbers on orders and emails, with 1,600+ carriers and their logos, a direct tracking link and a Track button. No account needed.
  • Vanquish Multiple Addresses for WooCommerce – give customers an address book: save multiple billing and shipping addresses and pick one at checkout.
